PMC Copyright notice PMCID: PMC12870302 PMID: 41634563 Abstract Improving alfalfa forage yieldis closely associated to the use of fertilizers. Generally, with the increase of fertilizer, alfalfa yield also increases correspondingly. However, in saline-alkaline areas, balancing the amount of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium and achieving a high alfalfa yield is of great importance. In this study, we assumed that the alfalfa yield would reach the maximum at a moderate proportion of multiple fertilizers. A five-year continuous multi-fertilizer experiment with different ratios was carried out in the North China Plain. The experiment used randomized complete block design, tested three fertilizers and four fertilization levels (N0 0 kg ha − 1 , N1 5 kg ha − 1 , N2 10 kg ha − 1 , N3 15 kg ha − 1 ; P0 0 kg ha − 1 , P1 30 kg ha − 1 , P2 60 kg ha − 1 , P3 90 kg ha − 1 ; K0 0 kg ha − 1 , K1 90 kg ha − 1 , K2 180 kg ha − 1 , K3 270 kg ha − 1 ), resulting in a total of 14 different treatments, N0P0K0, N0P2K2, N1P2K2, N1P1K2, N1P2K1, N2P1K1, N2P0K2, N2P1K2, N2P2K2, N2P3K2, N2P2K0, N2P2K1, N2P2K3, N3P2K2. All fertilizers applied twice a year. Results indicated that N2P1K2, N1P2K1 and N2P2K1 treatments had significant effects on increasing alfalfa dry matter and dry to fresh biomass; N2P2K2 treatment had a significant effect on alfalfa crude protein, but crude protein under N3P2K2 and N2P2K2 treatments showed no significant differences. In addition, the relative feed value (RFV) was significantly affected by potassium fertilizer. Under low potassium application, RFV showed a significant increase. N2 (10 kg ha − 1 ), P2 (60 kg ha − 1 ), and K2 (180 kg ha − 1 ) significantly increased the utilization efficiency of fertilizers, agronomic efficiency, and economic benefits, which were associated with decrease in fertilizer expenditure and increase in alfalfa income. The N3 (15 kg ha − 1 ), P3 (90 kg ha − 1 ), and K3 (270 kg ha − 1 ) significantly increased soil fertility, while had no significant effect on hay yield, nutritional quality and utilization efficiency. Therefore, N1P2K1 (5 kg ha − 1 N, 60 kg ha P − 1 , 90 kg ha P − 1 ) treatment in the saline-alkali areas of the North China Plain is recommended for achieving high alfalfa yield, forage nutritional content, and improving the utilization rate of fertilizers by plants, increasing the farmers’ income without compromising soil fertility. Keywords: Alfalfa, Salt tolerance, Fertility, Economic benefit Introduction Alfalfa ( Medicago sativa L.) is one of the most widely cultivated legume forage crops, globally. In China, it has become the dominant cultivated forage because of its desirable production performance, stress persistence, excellent nitrogen fixation and soil conversion ability [ 1 , 2 ]. In recent years, commercial alfalfa cultivated area in China has reached 6.3 × 10 5 hectare [ 3 ]. Studies have shown that forage yield and quality of alfalfa are strongly linked to nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K) fertilizers [ 3 , 4 ]. With the development of the animal husbandry, the demand for forage is increasing yearly. Therefore, excessive fertilizers are often applied to forage crops to achieve higher yields and short-term economic profits. However, it leads to excessive soil nutrient accumulation (N, P, K and other nutrients), soil compaction, low nutrient use efficiency, reduced forage quality, and increased environmental concerns [ 4 – 7 ]. Generally, forage crops that rely on excessive fertilization are not sustainable agriculture. Excessive N fertilizations are associated with public health risks, environmental concerns, and economic losses [ 8 ], such as nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions and water pollution by nitrate (NO 3 − ) leaching [ 9 ]. Moreover, poor N management leads to low nitrogen use efficiency, which is detrimental to soil health [ 10 ]. For instance, Singh et al. [ 11 ] pointed out that the N use efficiency in South Asia was 21.63% in 2018, while the N input proportion under the region was much higher, resulting in soil N deposition and annual financial losses. Moreover, Wang et al. [ 12 ] and Zhang et al. [ 13 ] demonstrated the N fertilizer application and biological N fixation had increased 100-fold, while global nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) had decreased from 60% to 46% from 1900 to 2000. Therefore, the amount of N fertilizer application should not be the key strategy for crop production but insteadthe use efficiency of N fertilizer should be focused. Generally, long-term P application is believed to increase potassium use efficiency (PUE), which in turn increases yield. The utilization efficiency of P in China is 10 ~ 25%, which is lower than N and K [ 14 ]. The primary reason for low P utilization is the easy fixation of P in soil. Phosphate is easy to combine with divalent and trivalent cations to form precipitates in the soil, which is difficult to circulate and migrate [ 15 ]. Consequently, plants will find it challenging to absorb and utilize the P element distant from their roots, reducing the effectiveness of P fertilizer. Moreover, the soil’s cohesive particles and aluminium-iron oxides will also physically adsorb N, P, and K, reducing their fluidity and fertilizer efficiency [ 16 ]. Therefore, appropriate phosphorus fertilization according to crop demands is essential for improving PUE and reducing losses. Potassium, as an essential and macronutrient, assists in the transport of water and nutrients in plants [ 17 ]. However, the effects of K have been over-exploited, as the amount of K input far exceeds its output [ 18 ]. Previous studies have shown that a significant quantity of K is reserved in the soil that cannot be utilized by crops, and continuous K fertilization would further enriche the soil K contents [ 17 , 18 ]. Wang et al. [ 19 ] indicated that the total K content in China is very high, and the content of unavailable K in soil is much higher than that of available potassium. At the same time, the increased application of K is still facing the dilemma of extremely low utilization rate by crops. In China, the potassium use efficiency is about 35%−50%, while the expenditure of K fertilizer occupied over 50% of income, resulting in resource and economic losses [ 20 ]. Studies have indicated that excessive fertilizers (N, P, and K) application can influence root growth, crop biomass distribution, and the colonization of rhizobia in leguminous crops, which can restrict the crops’ potential to absorb and utilize nutrients [ 21 – 23 ]. Therefore, optimizing the ratio of N, P, and K is essential for enhancing nutrient usage efficiency and ensuring economic benefits to promote sustainable pastoral agriculture production and animal husbandry development. Nevertheless, very few studies have focused on optimizing the ratios of N, P, and K fertilizer and their effects on the leguminous forage productivity, soil NPK surplus contents, and maximizing actual profits. We hypothesized that the optimal ratio of nitrogen, P, and K fertilizer can boost crop yield, improve plant fertilizer use, replenish soil NKP contents, and enhance economic revenue. To test the hypothesis, we conducted a five-year long-term field experiment to evaluate different ratios of NPK for alfalfa crop under saline-alkali soil condition. The objectives of the study were: (1) to analyze the inter-annual changes in soil N, P, and K input, output, and apparent balance during the five-year experiment; (2) to analyze the relationship between alfalfa yield, quality, and nutrient supply; and (3) to establish a suitable fertilization system for alfalfa based on environmental risks and economic benefits. Materials and methods Experimental site description A five-year (2015–2019) field experiment was conducted at the Fengmao Shengyuan Experimental Station (38°08′N, 117°51′E, 3.0 m above sea level) in Huanghua city, Hebei Province, North China. The North China Plain had a temperate monsoon climate, with average precipitation of 567.8 mm during the crop growihg period. The annual sunshine duration was 2461.9 h while the average annual temperature was 12.9 °C. No irrigation was carried out during the experimental period. Fig. 1 depicts the annual precipitation and mean temperature data collected from the local meteorological station of the experimental field. According to the World Reference Base Classification system, soil at the experimental soil is classified as clay soil (IUSS Working Group WRB, 2015) [ 15 ]. Before the commencement of experiment, the upper soil surface (20 cm) had the following physio-chemical properties: pH 8.18, organic matter 22.6 g/kg, soil alkali hydrolyzable N (Alk. The Alfalfa seedbed was prepared and established in 2015. A seedling rate of 15 kg h − 1 was used at a 2–3 cm sowing depth, and row spacing of 30 cm was maintained. The experiment was conducted for five consecutive years (from 2015 to 2019). The experiment was organized in a Randomized Complete Block (RCB) Design, with three fertilizer types (N, P, and K) and four fertilization levels (N0 0 kg ha − 1 ,N1 5 kg ha − 1 ,N2 10 kg ha − 1 , N3 15 kg ha − 1 ; P0 0 kg ha − 1 , P1 30 kg ha − 1 , P2 60 kg ha − 1 , P3 90 kg ha − 1 ; K0 0 kg ha, K1 90 kg ha − 1 , K2 180 kg ha − 1 , K3 270 kg/ha − 1 ).These fertilizers were used together in different ratios comprising a total of 14 different treatments and there were three replicates per treatment (Table 1 ). N0P0K0 was used as the blank control treatment. Urea ( N ≥ 46.4%), ammonium phosphate (P 2 O 5 ≥ 12%), and potassium sulfate (K 2 O ≥ 52%) were used as fertilizers sources. Fertilizers were applied twice a year (50% after the first harvest, as basic fertilization; and 50% prior to 2rd, 3rd and 4th harvest, as after manuring). Table 1. Neutral detergent fiber (NDF, %) and acid detergent fiber (ADF, %) was determined according to NY/T1459-2007 and GB/T20806-2006 standards [ 20 ], respectively. The relative feed value (RFV) was calculated from dry matter digestibility (DMD) and dry matter intake (DMI) using ADF (%) and NDF (%), respectively (Ferreira et al., 2015): Soil sampling, measurements and calculations Soil samples were randomly taken at a depth of 20 cm with a soil corer (5 cm diameter) before sowing and after the last harvest during 2015–2019. For each treatment, samples were collected at three different locations within each plot. Samples were then analyzed for available soil N, Olsen-P and available K. Soil available nitrogen was determined by Kjeldahl’s nitrogen determination method, Olsen-P was determined by sodium bicarbonate extraction-molybdenum antimony anti-colorimetric method (Westerman, 1990), and available K was determined by ammonium acetate extraction-flame photometric method (Bao, 2008). Economic benefits analysis The inputs materials (i.e., seeds, pesticide, farm machinery, labor, seedling transplanting, pruning, fertilizer application, and harvest) were assumed to be the same in different treatments. The output value of alfalfa was calculated based on the seven-year average market price. We used the alfalfa output value minus the total fertiliser cost in each treatment to represent the net income. The average price of alfalfa was 2.2 (RMB kg − 1 ), urea was 2.2 (RMB kg − 1 ), ammonium phosphate was 2.5 (RMB kg − 1 ), and potassium sulfate was 3.5 (RMB kg − 1 ). The values were converted from Chinese currency (¥) to US $ using the average official exchange rate (1 $=6.5973 ¥). The fertilizer type and levels were considered as fixed factors, year as a repetitive factor, and replication as a random factor. Significant differences among treatment means were determined based on the Duncan test at P < 0.05 level. The relationships of forage yield and qualitative indexes with treatments under different years were checked for normality, and linear and nonlinear regression analyses were performed. Result Effects of different fertilizer treatments on forage yield Alfalfa yield was significantly ( P < 0.05) influenced by NKP fertilizer treatments, type and year. In the first year, alfalfa yield under N1P1K2 fertilization was the highest, the lowest yield data appeared under N0P2K2 and N2P0K2 treatments (Fig. 2 a); In 2016, the highest yield of single alfalfa appeared under N1P2K1 treatment, and the lowest yield of alfalfa under N2P1K2 fertilization was found under all treatments (Fig. 2 b). The yield of alfalfa in the following year was different, with the highest value appearing in N2P2K0 and N1P1K2, and the lowest in the control group, that is, without fertilization treatment (Fig. 2 c). The output value of alfalfa in 2018 was not significantly affected by fertilization, and in the last year, 2019, the output value of alfalfa was significantly affected by different fertilization combinations, with the highest value appearing under N2P3K2, N2P2K0, N2P2K1, N2P2K3, N1P1K2 and N1P2K1 (Fig. 2 d and e). What’s more, the inter-annual yield variation shows a trend of first rising and then decreasing, that is, the yield reaches its best on three to four years after planting (Table S1, S2). N3P2K2, N2P3K2 and N2P2K3 had no significant difference in the yield of alfalfa in five years compared with N0P0K0. At the same time, in the two consecutive years of planting in 2018 and 2019, there was no advantage for the growth of plant yield compared with low concentrations of N0P2K2, N2P0K2 and N2P1K2. In general, N2P2K0, N1P1K2 and N1P2K1 showed significant differences ( P < 0.05) in the yield growth of alfalfa compared with the control group during the five-year yield accumulation. Fig. 2.
